title: Yigdal
attribution: The Hebrew hymn Yigdal is attributed to Daniel ben Judah of Rome (about 1404). The tune is the old Friday-evening synagogue melody of London's Great Synagogue, made famous by its cantor Myer Lyon ("Leoni", died 1797) and borrowed in 1770 for the English hymn "The God of Abraham Praise"; notation after the Jewish Encyclopedia (1906). First four lines. Both public domain.
